newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says very heavy vote on draft constitution.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says very heavy vote on draft constitution.

text.p: Official media said Algerians on Thursday flooded polling stations to vote in a constitutional referendum that appeared to be passing without the attacks threatened by Islamic militants.
More than two hours before polls were to close, nearly three-quarters of Algeria's 16.4 million eligible voters had cast ballots, Algerian state-run radio said, quoting the interior ministry.
Official media said voting was taking place peacefully and there were no reports of violence.

Residents in the garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, said the army shelled mountains neary the city on Wednesday night, apparently trying to pre-empt any buildup of Moslem guerrillas. Blida is a route for Moslem guerrillas seeking to carry out attacks around Algiers.
The national turnout was 71.94 percent at about 6 p.m (1700 GMT), compared to 65.82 percent in last year's presidential election at the same time, official figures showed.
However, Algerian radio said turnout was low in two northeastern Berber provinces where a Berber-dominated party had called for a boycott.
Moslem rebels, waging a five-year guerrilla war against the North African country's secular government, had vowed to disrupt the poll and warned Algerians not to vote.

Opposition parties either called for a boycott or urged a "no" vote on the changes, which would strengthen the position of President Liamine Zeroual and bar Islamic fundamentalists from seeking election.
Residents said they saw many "Yes" ballots thrown away near polling stations in Algiers, apparently by voters opposed to the proposed constitution.
